new.notes: Exact-source ITEM assessment https://github.com/CultureBotAI/HabitatMech/issues/1454 (20261012T111107Z-saline_spring_sediment). The qualified deep-subsurface groundwater branch names saline spring sediment. This is particulate material, not a subtype of the enclosing groundwater material. The single later organism example is Zodletone_IIa from Zodletone Spring, not a new source of universal chemical measurements. Sediment is a defensible broad candidate; saline-permeated sediment requires additional porespace evidence. The CLASS-only ungrounded disposition is not an ITEM identity assessment. Retain the qualified mint under ENVO:00002007 sediment, not an exact identity. The sediment genus follows the deposited material meaning and inspected source descriptions. Marine-water-column deposition and currently saline porespace are not universally established; do not impose those tighter genera. No authored definition is added to this NARROW record. Original member provenance remains unavailable and shared endpoint issue #1398 remains open. Source accounting and unrelated records must be preserved.

causal_graphs.title: Seawater DOM oligotrophic uptake
causal_graphs.description: Dissolved organic matter in seawater creates dilute carbon pools that select for oligotrophic bacteria with streamlined genomes and efficient nutrient transport systems.

edges.subject: sea_water
edges.description: The seawater carbon pool contains dissolved organic matter used by marine microbes.

evidence.snippet: largest pools of reduced carbon on Earth
evidence.notes: Moran and colleagues describe ocean dissolved organic matter as a large reduced-carbon reservoir.

edges.subject: dissolved_organic_matter
edges.description: Ocean dissolved organic molecules are produced and consumed by members of the marine microbiome.

evidence.notes: Moran and colleagues frame ocean DOM cycling as molecular relationships between DOM compounds and the microbes that produce and consume them.

edges.subject: low_organic_carbon_availability
edges.description: Low seawater carbon concentrations select for oligotrophic bacterial growth strategies.

evidence.notes: Lauro and colleagues compare marine bacteria adapted to low- and high-nutrient trophic habitats.

edges.subject: nutrient_transport_systems
edges.description: Nutrient transporter architecture controls uptake of dilute substrates by oligotrophic bacteria.

evidence.notes: Norris and colleagues model copiotroph-oligotroph differences as a consequence of nutrient-transporter trade-offs.

edges.subject: oligotrophic_marine_bacteria
edges.description: Prototypical marine oligotrophs rely on ATP-binding cassette transporters for nutrient uptake.

evidence.notes: Norris and colleagues contrast SAR11-like oligotrophs with copiotrophs that encode phosphotransferase systems.

edges.subject: dilute_nutrient_uptake
edges.description: Uptake of dilute organic substrates enables heterotrophic bacteria to participate in ocean DOM cycling.

evidence.snippet: optimal nutrient uptake and metabolic strategy
evidence.notes: Norris and colleagues connect nutrient-uptake strategy to marine heterotroph metabolism.

edges.subject: oligotrophic_marine_bacteria
edges.description: Highly abundant oligotrophic seawater bacteria show genome streamlining.

evidence.snippet: Genome streamlining in a cosmopolitan oceanic bacterium
evidence.notes: Giovannoni and colleagues described genome streamlining in the cosmopolitan seawater bacterium SAR11.

curation_history.changes: Added a seawater dissolved-organic-matter and oligotrophic-uptake graph backed by PMID:26951682, PMID:19805210, PMID:34010286, and PMID:16109880.

old.notes: Definition authored from the record's committed deep-research report under research/habitats/, read in full; the report's proposed sentence, genus and near-miss table are the evidence. No new research was commissioned. Labelled for the setting, not the organism: the report is explicit that 'Seaweed' names an organism, which FOODON:03412266 already does, while the concept here is a benthic place. Modelled on the sibling ENVO:01000059 'sea grass bed'. REPLACE because the inherited ENVO:00001999 'marine water body' is not broader - a bed underlies a water body rather than being a kind of one.
